app.title: Conference paper review workspace
app.summary: The reviewer reads a submitted paper on one side of the screen and fills in the venue's review form on the other. While writing, they select sentences in the paper and drop them into the review as quotes, tagged with the section they came from, and the paper highlights every passage the review still quotes. They score the paper, rate fixed criteria with a sentence each, and tick a guidelines checklist, while a word count against their own target and a list of what is still missing tell them when the review is ready. The draft saves as they type and comes out as plain text in the order the submission form wants, copied or downloaded.

task.text: Write a defensible review of one paper against a venue's form and checklist, grounded in quotes from the paper itself.

data.text: One long structured paper split into numbered sections and figure captions, plus the reviewer's scores, criterion ratings, checklist ticks and free review text, with the passages quoted from the paper.
data.item: a paragraph or figure caption of a submitted paper, and the review written about it

stage.text: peer review of a submitted paper

mechanism.text: A document reader and a review form sit side by side; selecting text in the reader raises a button that inserts the passage, with its section, at the cursor in the review, and the reader highlights whatever the review still quotes. The form recomputes word counts and a list of unfinished items on every change, saves to the browser, and exports the review as ordered plain text.

field.text: peer review of HCI conference papers in accessibility

workflow.name: write a structured review of one document, quoting from it

steps.step: read the document section by section
steps.here: The submission is shown in a reader pane with a sticky menu of its numbered sections; paragraphs and figure captions are the units that can be quoted.

steps.step: pull a selected passage into the draft, with where it came from
steps.here: Selecting text in the paper raises a 'Quote into review' button that inserts the passage as a '>' quote line, followed by its section number or figure caption, at the cursor in the review; the paper then highlights every passage the review still quotes.
The review text box takes the reviewer's own prose around the quotes; words on quote lines are counted apart from the reviewer's own words.
Radio scales for the overall recommendation (1 to 5) and the reviewer's expertise (1 to 4), then originality, significance, rigour and clarity each rated Low, Medium or High with a one-sentence note.

steps.step: tick off each point on a fixed checklist
steps.here: Seven checks from the reviewer guidelines (anonymisation, ethics, participants, figure descriptions, limitations, contribution type, open materials) are ticked once verified in the paper.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: A meter fills toward a 500-word target for the reviewer's own words, and a list under 'Before you paste it into PCS' names every unset score, unrated or unnoted criterion, short text and unticked check.
One button copies the review as plain text in the submission form's order (recommendation, expertise, review text, then each criterion with its note); another downloads the same text as a .txt file.

distinctive: Each quote carries the section or figure-caption label it came from, and the paper highlights only the passages still quoted in the review, so deleting a quote removes its highlight and the reviewer sees which parts the review covers.
The reviewer's own words are counted separately from quoted words and measured against a self-set word target rather than the venue's.
Every criterion rating needs a one-sentence justification, so the overall recommendation can be defended criterion by criterion.
The plain-text export follows the order of the submission system's form, so it can be pasted straight in.
The draft, quotes and checklist save to the browser on every change, with the time of the last save shown.
